speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have a longstanding pruritic rash accompanied by numbness and tingling in your palms. To help me pinpoint the cause, have you noticed any specific triggers like exposure to chemicals, new soaps, or jewelry, and does the rash appear on the backs of your hands or fingers as well?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Paraneoplastic Pemphigus secondary to Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (likely MALT lymphoma of the lung), given the triad of severe, photosensitive rash, acral sensory neuropathy (numbness/tingling), and significant exposure to agricultural dusts/chemicals which are risk factors for lymphoproliferative disorders. I request immediate CBC, ANA, SSA, SSB, and a CT Chest/PET scan.
